approachQuestion.prompt:
Longest Cable Route. Parent-child connections of a non-empty binary tree are unit-length cables. Return the greatest number of cables on any simple route between two nodes. Endpoints may be anywhere; the route need not include the root and cannot repeat a node. Return only a length.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 0(1(2(4(-,-),-),3(-,5(-,-))),-). Output: 4, along 4→2→1→3→5. Example 2: Input: 8(-,9(-,10(-,-))). Output: 2. Example 3: Input: 6(-,-). Output: 0.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; labels are signed 32-bit integers and may repeat. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles, shared nodes, or extra connections. Shape is unrestricted; all cables have the same length.

options.text: Use explicit postorder frames. A completed child returns its longest downward distance. Combine both child arms into a route through each node, update a global best, and return only the longer arm upward.
options.feedback: Every route has a highest node, at which its two sides enter different child subtrees. One arm can be extended upward; both arms form a complete candidate.

options.text: At every node, run fresh traversals of both child subtrees to measure their heights, combine the two arms through that node, and keep the greatest candidate.
options.feedback: All possible meeting nodes are checked, so the result is correct. Fresh height scans repeatedly visit overlapping subtrees; returning heights once removes that work.

options.text: Combine only the longest left and right arms through the root.
options.feedback: Example 1 has best root route length 3, but a route entirely below it has length 4.

options.text: Return twice the greatest root-to-leaf distance in cables.
options.feedback: Example 2 has root-to-leaf distance 2 and only 2 cables total; doubling gives 4 by inventing a second branch.

feedback.reason: Distinguish one downward arm returned to a parent from a complete two-arm route.
details: Use postorder frames. A missing child has height -1 and a leaf has height 0, measured in cables. With child heights L and R, update a global maximum with L+R+2, then return 1+max(L,R) to the parent. Release child frames after passing their fixed-size results. Return the global maximum.

A path through a node joins the best left and right downward paths. Return only the longer downward height to its parent; returning the whole diameter would incorrectly allow a branching path to branch again.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed single postorder traversal let n be the node count and h the longest root-to-leaf path length in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case pair. Count frames, partial child heights, and the global best; exclude the input and scalar result. No route arrays or table of completed heights are retained.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: One height combine per node updates the best route using height-bounded frames.
details: Each node has a fixed number of frame transitions and one combine. One active ancestor chain holds O(h) fixed-size frames; a chain attains h live frames.

Every route has a unique highest node. At that node the best route uses the longest available arm in each child subtree; maximizing these candidates covers all routes. Only one arm can extend to a parent without repeating a node.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each node has a fixed number of frame transitions and one combine. One active ancestor chain holds O(h) fixed-size frames; a chain attains h live frames.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
